title: Compliance for small companies - the employee-count threshold explained
p1:
Think having just 9 employees means your company has fewer compliance responsibilities?

That assumption could cost your business more than you expect.

Many founders believe employment laws apply only after a company reaches a certain size. But the reality is more complicated.
p2:
Here's the surprising part: different labour laws can have different employee-count thresholds.

For example, under India's labour law framework, certain requirements may apply when an establishment reaches 10 employees, while others may begin at 20 or even higher.

And crossing a threshold can trigger new responsibilities, even if your business is still relatively small.
p3:
This is why tracking employee strength is more than an HR exercise.

A company should regularly review its headcount, identify which laws apply to its establishment, and check whether new obligations arise as its workforce grows.

One practical tip: don't wait until you hire your next employee to investigate compliance. Review the applicable thresholds in advance. Also check whether the law counts contract workers, employees across locations, or only certain categories of workers. The answer can vary depending on the legislation.
conclusion: Founders and HR professionals: do you review legal compliance every time your employee count increases, or only when a problem arises? What employee-count threshold do you think small businesses most often overlook?
